questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: The outside of the curve
The inside of the curve
Wherever traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose your lane position based on current conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: For motorcycle operators, eye protection is:

options.text: Required.
Not required, but recommended.
Not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle operators must wear proper eye protection when riding in Georgia.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Move closer to the vehicle in front of you so you can use its lights to see farther down the road.
Keep riding at your normal speed to lower the risk of being struck from behind.
Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed and increase your following distance at night. You can see less at night, so you need more time and space to react to hazards ahead.

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Not return to your original lane until you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
Return to your original lane as soon as the truck is behind you.
Return to your original lane when you feel you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not return to your original lane until you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only return to your original lane after you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders.
Turn just your head.
Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: Look through a turn by turning just your head. Keep your shoulders still and your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: If the front wheel locks, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake immediately, then re-apply the brake.
Release the front brake immediately and only use the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you come to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately, then re-apply the brake.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake right away and re-apply it.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road indicates:

options.text: No parking is permitted.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They show traffic laws for that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Provide a narrow view of the road behind you.
Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
Are illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors do. Objects appear farther away than they really are. Take time to adjust to convex mirrors on your motorcycle.

questions.question: There is the greatest potential for conflict between a motorcycle and other traffic:

options.text: On the highway.
At intersections.
On rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where motorcycles are most likely to have conflicts with other vehicles. Be extra careful when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Use the road shoulder to slow down before crossing.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Ride straight ahead in your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight ahead in your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: Ride straight ahead in your lane to cross angled railroad or trolley tracks. If you change your angle, you may drift into another lane and hit oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When riding over scored pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look down to see the road surface changes.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Stay to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding over scored pavement in a work zone. Ride slowly, keep a steady throttle, and don't fight the handlebars.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the center of the lane:

options.text: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
The driver will have trouble seeing you.
You should avoid this position.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than their side mirrors, so this position makes it more likely they will see you.

questions.question: When taking a curve while riding in a group, use what formation?

options.text: A single-file line.
Pairs.
A staggered line.

questions.correctAnswerText: A single-file line.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation in general. Switch to a single-file line when turning, taking a curve, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve away from a hazard, press gently on the handgrip on the side where you want to escape.

questions.question: When being passed on your left, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Ride on the right side of the lane.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed on your left. If you move to the right, the passing driver may re-enter your lane too quickly and hit you.

questions.question: About the oily strip in the center of a traffic lane, motorcyclists should:

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
Not worry about the oil and grease.
Find the lane with the least oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding on oil and grease buildup. The oily strip is usually less than two feet wide, so you can stay on the left or right side of the oil and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Make a 45 to 90 degree angle with the curb.
Not have any wheel or fender touching the curb.
Be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make a 45 to 90 degree angle with the curb.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle parked on the road should make a 45 to 90 degree angle with the curb, with a wheel or fender touching the curb.

questions.question: Helmets are:

options.text: Required for all riders.
Recommended but not required.
Required only for new riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet every time they ride. A helmet is the best protection against head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: If wearing a jacket for protection in hot weather, you should:

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool off.
Remove the jacket to stay cool in the sun.
Keep the jacket on to protect yourself.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the jacket on to protect yourself.
questions.explanation: A good riding jacket protects you in a crash, no matter the weather. In hot weather, jackets also help prevent dehydration. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep the rider from overheating.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that the road will be divided ahead.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How quickly the alcohol is consumed
How often the person consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: BAC depends on body weight, how much alcohol is consumed, and how fast it is consumed. How often someone drinks does not affect BAC. Never ride after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: The oily strip down the center of a lane:

options.text: Should only be traveled upon if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.
Usually provides adequate traction for riding, unless it is raining.
Should be avoided at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually provides adequate traction for riding, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The center strip of the road is usually oily but provides enough grip for safe riding, except when it rains. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it while staying in the center of the lane.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride more slowly than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Cover the clutch and the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and the brakes.
questions.explanation: When approaching an intersection, ride with care. Keep your hand near the clutch and both brakes so you can react quickly if needed.

questions.question: If traveling with a load, the load should be:

options.text: Secured as low as possible.
Secured as high as possible.
Attached to a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads low if not using saddlebags. Attaching a load to a sissy bar raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and can throw off the balance.
